newsitem.title: USA: Interstate Bakeries profits triple in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Interstate Bakeries profits triple in quarter.

text.p: Interstate Bakeries Corp., the largest U.S. baker and distributor of fresh branded bread and cakes, said Thursday its quarterly profits more than tripled as price hikes helped it offset higher ingredient costs.

The company, whose brands include Holsum, Merita, Wonder and Home Pride, said its profits surged to $18.7 million, or 49 cents a share, in the first quarter ended Aug. 24. That compares with $5.7 million, or 21 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
Sales jumped to $753.6 million from $471.4 million.

While escalating ingredient prices were a concern in the quarter, recent trends in the commodity markets indicate the worst may be over, said Charles Sullivan, chairman of the Kansas City, Mo.-based company.
"Though we have little control over commodity prices, as a major food company we are capable of taking appropriate action to protect our profit margins."
Interstate Bakeries acquired Continental Baking from Ralston Purina Co. in July.
The company's stock jumped $3.50 to $36.50 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
